sentences.text: Marta S. Fernández named the genus Mollesaurus in 1999, designating Mollesaurus periallus as the type species — the specific specimen the species is based on.
Fossils of this animal were discovered near the city of Zapala in the Neuquén Basin.
Mollesaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
It is classified within the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
While initially considered a species of Ophthalmosaurus, recent cladistic analyses confirm Mollesaurus is a valid genus of ophthalmosaurid.

Druckenmiller and Maxwell (2010) identified Mollesaurus as the most basal member of the ophthalmosaurid lineage containing Brachypterygius, Caypullisaurus, and Platypterygius, excluding Ophthalmosaurus.
A 2012 study by Fischer et al. placed Mollesaurus as the most basal member of the subfamily Ophthalmosaurinae.
Mollesaurus lived during the early Bajocian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 171.6 to 170 million years ago.
The time range for Mollesaurus is the Bajocian stage, spanning from 170.9 to 168.6 million years ago.
